title: Modified on One Branch, Deleted on Another
objective: Resolve a modify/delete conflict by accepting the deliberate removal of an obsolete file.
description: Main updates legacy.txt while feature/cleanup removes it. During the merge, decide that the obsolete file should stay deleted, mark that resolution, and finish the merge commit.

lesson.principle: A modify/delete conflict is a decision about whether the file should still exist, not a line-by-line edit.
lesson.question: The feature branch deliberately removes obsolete legacy.txt. Which command records that choice during the merge?
lesson.explanation: git rm removes the file from the worktree and stages the deletion, allowing the merge commit to keep it deleted.
pitfalls: Restoring legacy.txt and accidentally rejecting the intended deletion.
Deleting the file manually without staging the removal.
Stopping before the merge commit is created.

hints: Run git merge feature/cleanup and inspect git status. Git reports a modify/delete conflict for legacy.txt.
The feature branch intentionally removes the obsolete file. Use git rm legacy.txt to keep that deletion.
Run git commit, then git-conflict-lab check to verify the merge and the file removal.
